- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.15) — model fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays response to sentiment shifts, especially after sharp spikes — correct by adding 1–2 days of lagged sentiment adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows; apply smoothing or decay filter to sentiment-weighted moving averages.
- Overshoot after spikes: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model continues upward — reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — cap forecast growth to 10% above 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
